observations: reprotest compares repeated builds under controlled environmental variations and reports artifact differences.
Its documented variation surface includes environment, build path, kernel, CPU count, time, user/group, file ordering, hostname/domain, HOME, locales, executable path, timezone and umask.
Reproducible Builds explicitly identifies timestamps, file ordering and permissions/umask as archive reproducibility hazards.
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH provides a deterministic source-derived timestamp contract and requires build processes to use it instead of current time when embedded timestamps are needed.
ZIP archives carry per-member modification timestamps and may carry extra metadata; Python ZipInfo exposes date_time and archive attributes that can be set explicitly.
reprotest itself has environment/privilege complexity and documented variation caveats; importing it as an F2 runtime dependency would add unnecessary surface for this narrow release gate.
source_grounded_conclusion: The useful donor is the variance-testing method, not the whole reprotest runtime. WP1107 should gain a deterministic archive builder and a bounded variance matrix that perturbs only release-relevant environmental dimensions, then compares complete archive bytes/hash plus manifest identity.
counterhypothesis: The existing WP1107 manifest verifier may already be sufficient because it proves payload file bytes independent of ZIP container metadata; byte-identical ZIP generation could add complexity without improving handoff integrity.
next_discriminator: Map whether archive-container nondeterminism can change the handed-off ZIP while all WP1107 payload-manifest checks remain green; if yes, container-level reproducibility is a distinct integrity property.
